skills.name: code-review-and-quality
skills.description: Review a proposed or completed change when the user explicitly requests code review. Evaluate correctness, maintainability, tests, security, compatibility, and evidence; do not edit unless fixes are separately requested.

skills.name: code-simplification
skills.description: Simplify existing code when the user explicitly requests a behavior-preserving clarity refactor. Reduce unnecessary complexity and duplication while preserving public contracts, errors, side effects, compatibility, and verified behavior.

skills.name: context-engineering
skills.description: Improve agent instructions, skill routing, task context, or handoffs when the user explicitly requests context optimization, stale-guidance repair, or session recovery. Keep durable guidance aligned with current repository evidence.

skills.name: documentation-and-adrs
skills.description: Write or revise technical documentation or an architecture decision record when the user explicitly requests it. Ground claims in repository evidence, distinguish current from proposed behavior, and record settled trade-offs.

skills.name: doubt-driven-development
skills.description: Adversarially challenge a named high-risk product or technical decision when the user explicitly requests it. Compare evidence, assumptions, failure modes, reversibility, and safe experiments; do not use for routine uncertainty.

skills.name: idea-refine
skills.description: Refine a product, architecture, tooling, or workflow idea when the user explicitly asks to ideate, compare directions, or stress-test it before commitment. Frame goals, alternatives, trade-offs, risks, and unresolved decisions.

skills.name: incremental-implementation
skills.description: Implement exactly one authorized, self-contained task packet per explicit invocation, verify it, update its checklist and handoff, then stop for review. Commit the completed previous packet only with explicit commit authorization.

skills.name: interview-me
skills.description: Run a structured requirements interview when the user explicitly asks to be interviewed, grilled, or guided through unresolved decisions. Use available Prompt MCP tools, checkpoint committed answers, and stop before downstream work.

skills.name: performance-optimization
skills.description: Diagnose or improve a measured latency, throughput, memory, startup, size, cost, or CI problem when the user explicitly requests optimization or provides regression evidence. Preserve correctness and do not optimize from guesswork.

skills.name: planning-and-task-breakdown
skills.description: Create an implementation plan or review-gated task breakdown when the user explicitly requests planning, decomposition, milestones, or execution packets. Ground architecture and verification in repository evidence; do not implement.

skills.name: project-docs-maintainer
skills.description: Maintain a project documentation set when the user explicitly asks to organize, update, consolidate, or audit project knowledge. Preserve authoritative ownership, verified behavior, links, history, and audience boundaries.

skills.name: project-pull-request
skills.description: Create, update, or review a pull request when the user explicitly requests PR work. Discover repository policy, base/head, templates, checks, and provider state; preserve unrelated changes and require authority for external mutations.

skills.name: project-release
skills.description: Prepare, publish, verify, or recover a release when the user explicitly requests release work. Require a confirmed SemVer, discover repository policy, verify artifacts and trust evidence, and separate preparation from publication.

skills.name: security-and-hardening
skills.description: Audit or harden a concrete trust boundary when the user explicitly requests security work or identifies a defect. Cover inputs, privileges, secrets, dependencies, filesystem/process boundaries, failure behavior, and verification.

skills.name: spec-driven-development
skills.description: Define or revise an implementation-ready specification when the user explicitly requests substantial specification work. Use recoverable Prompt MCP decisions, persist non-sensitive answers, require draft approval, and stop before planning.
